connections.why: Changes in the family and in social values are part of the same shift in how society is organised
The digital/cyber world has transformed how music and the arts are produced and shared
Changing family and social structures connect to how migrant communities integrate
Heritage, festivals and the cultural life of a city are all expressions of artistic identity
Popular music and the arts are often a vehicle for youth political engagement and protest
Immigration leads directly into the challenges and processes of integration
Successful integration is the answer to the marginalisation and racism migrants can face
Immigration is one of the most politically contested issues in public life
Young people's right to vote and engage shapes wider political movements and protest
Demonstrations, strikes and historic political shifts are how citizens exercise political power
Volunteering / equal rights / youth issues feed directly into political engagement
The set texts and films illuminate the social themes of family and values studied earlier
Many set texts and films explore immigration, identity and marginalisation
Set works often dramatise political conflict, protest and historical upheaval
Close analysis skills built on the set text transfer to the independent research project
Cultural and regional topics make rich subjects for the student-chosen research project
